Under every interleaving of put!/take!/iterate/fetch/wait/close/empty! tasks on a channel of any size, the values of completed put! calls equal, as a multiset, the values received by take!/iterate plus those still buffered plus those discarded by empty!: no item is lost or duplicated.
A channel never stores more than sz_max items (an unbuffered one stores none), under every interleaving.
A step of a fetch task never changes the buffer, and a value fetch returns is the first buffered item.
Once a channel is closed no task is queued on its conditions, and every task still blocked in a channel operation is a taker already chosen by an unbuffered put! that will hand it its value.
take! on a closed channel with an empty buffer throws the close exception (InvalidStateException after close(c)) without blocking.
iterate(c) returns nothing only when the channel is closed and its buffer is empty, so for x in c sees every item.

A task sleeps on a channel condition only while its operation cannot proceed or a woken put! that will let it proceed has not yet run (buffered: takers sleep only on an empty buffer, putters only when buffer plus woken putters fill it; unbuffered: put! and take! never both sleep unpaired; wait(c) sleeps only with no pending put!).
For an unbuffered channel, isready(c) holds exactly when some task is in a put! waiting for a taker.
